Rule 71 — Verdicts

norms.text:
In every issue for the recovery of money only, or specific real or personal property, the jury shall render a general verdict.

#### Committee Note – 1959

This Rule is the same as Section 107 of the 1943 Code (Section 510.230, RSMo 1959).

This rule is the same as original proposed Rule 22.02(a). Paragraph (b) of the proposed Rule 22.02 provided for a discretionary special verdict in the form of special findings on each issue of fact, and for submission to a jury of special interrogatories. Paragraph (b) is omitted for these reasons: (1) it is a radical change in the existing practice; (2) experience with similar provisions has not been uniformly satisfactory; (3) the Bar overwhelmingly opposed the discretionary special verdict system in all cases.

norms.heading: Jury Shall Assess Amount of Recovery, When

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 71 — Verdicts

norms.text:
When a verdict shall be found for the plaintiff in an action for the recovery of money only, the jury shall also assess the amount of recovery; so, also, if they find for the defendant in case of a counterclaim, crossclaim or other demand for money. A verdict shall meet the requirements of this rule if the jury returns a finding of the total amount of the damages and assesses percentages of fault.
When exemplary or punitive damages are allowed by the jury, the amount thereof shall be separately stated in the verdict. When both damages for personal injuries and damages to property are allowed by the jury, the verdict shall state separately the amount allowed for the aggregate of the items of damage connected with the personal injury and the amount allowed for the aggregate of the items of damage connected with the injury to the property.

#### Committee Note – 1959

This Rule is Section 111 of the 1943 Code (Section 510.270, RSMo 1959) with a new sentence added and provision made for counter-claims and cross-claims instead of "offsets." ... This new sentence provides that the damages for personal injury and property damage be stated separately in the verdict. This will be of great help in cases involving subrogation rights and in tax computations.
(Amended October 16, 1986, effective July 1, 1987.)

norms.heading: Motion for a Directed Verdict and for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 72 — Motion for a Directed Verdict and for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict

norms.text:
(a) Motion for Directed Verdict: When Made: Effect. A party may move for a directed verdict at the close of the evidence offered by an opponent. The filing of such motion does not constitute a waiver of movant's right to offer evidence to the same extent as if the motion had not been made. A motion which is not granted is not a waiver of trial by jury even though all parties to the action have moved for directed verdicts. A motion for a directed verdict shall state the specific grounds therefor. The order of the court granting a motion for a directed verdict is effective without any assent of the jury.
(b) Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict. A party may move for a directed verdict at the close of all the evidence. Whenever such motion is denied or for any reason is not granted, the court is deemed to have submitted the action to the jury subject to a later determination of the legal questions raised by the motion.
Not later than thirty days after entry of judgment, a party who has moved for a directed verdict may move to have the verdict and any judgment entered thereon set aside and to have judgment entered in accordance with the motion for a directed verdict; or if a verdict was not returned, such party, within thirty days after the jury has been discharged, may move for judgment in accordance with the motion for a directed verdict.
A motion for a new trial may be joined with this motion, or a new trial may be prayed for in the alternative. If a verdict was returned the court may allow the judgment to stand or may reopen the judgment and either order a new trial or direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed. If no verdict was returned the court may direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed or may order a new trial.
(c) Same: Conditional Rulings on Grant of Motion.
(1) If the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict provided for in subdivision (b) of this Rule, is granted, the court shall also rule on the motion for a new trial, if any, by determining whether it should be granted if the judgment is thereafter vacated or reversed, and shall specify the grounds for granting or denying the motion for the new trial.
If the motion for a new trial is thus conditionally granted, the order thereon does not affect the finality of the judgment. In case the motion for a new trial has been conditionally granted and the judgment is reversed on appeal, the new trial shall proceed unless the appellate court has otherwise ordered. In case the motion for new trial has been conditionally denied, the respondent on appeal may assert error in that denial; and if the judgment is reversed on appeal, subsequent proceedings shall be in accordance with the order of the appellate court.
(2) The party whose judgment has been set aside on the motion for judgment notwithstanding verdict, may upon appeal from the resulting adverse judgment, in addition to urging that the trial court erred in sustaining the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict, also brief and argue and the appellate court may determine, whether the appellant is, in any event, entitled to a new trial.
(d) Same: Denial of Motion. If the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict is denied, the party who prevailed on that motion, as respondent, may assert grounds entitling the party to a new trial in the event the appellate court concludes that the trial court erred in denying the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict. If the appellate court reverses the judgment, nothing in this Rule 72.01 precludes it from determining that the respondent is entitled to a new trial or from directing the court to determine whether a new trial shall be granted.

norms.heading: Trial Without Jury or With an Advisory Jury – Procedures

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 73 — Trial by Court

norms.text:
In cases tried without a jury or with an advisory jury:

(a) The court shall rule upon all objections to evidence as in jury cases. Where the evidence is ruled inadmissible, the court upon request shall take and record the evidence in full, unless it clearly appears that the evidence is not admissible on any ground or that the evidence is privileged.
(b) After the plaintiff has completed presentation of plaintiff's evidence, the defendant may move by motion for a judgment on the grounds that upon the facts and the law the plaintiff is not entitled to relief. The filing of such motion does not constitute a waiver of defendant's right to offer evidence.

(c) The court shall render the judgment it thinks proper under the law and the evidence.
If a party so requests, the court shall dictate to the court reporter or prepare and file a brief opinion containing a statement of the grounds for its decision and the method of deciding any damages awarded.

The court may, or if requested by a party shall, include in the opinion findings on the controverted material fact issues specified by the party. Any request for an opinion or findings of fact shall be made on the record before the introduction of evidence at trial or at such later time as the court may allow.
All fact issues upon which no specific findings are made shall be considered as having been found in accordance with the result reached.

(d) Except as provided in Rule 78.07(c), a party may, but need not, file a motion for new trial or a motion to amend the judgment or opinion, or both, as provided by Rule 78.04.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confie au juge la décision sur le faux, tout en permettant de statuer séparément sur les autres chefs de demande. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le jugement selon le droit et la preuve ainsi que les jugements portant sur certaines demandes seulement, sans règle spécifique sur le faux documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns the forgery issue to the judge while allowing the remaining claims to be decided separately. Missouri rules address judgment under the law and evidence and judgments on fewer than all claims, but contain no specific rule for documentary forgery.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux deux époux de demander expressément et conjointement que le juge n’énonce pas leurs torts et griefs dans les motifs, celui-ci constatant seulement les faits constitutifs d’une cause de divorce. Les §§ 452.320 et 452.305 imposent une constatation judiciaire du caractère irrémédiablement rompu du mariage et, le cas échéant, de faits justificatifs, sans prévoir cette dispense conjointe ; la Rule 73.01 concerne plus généralement les motifs et constatations du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows both spouses expressly and jointly to ask the judge not to state their faults and grievances in the reasoning, limiting the decision to finding facts constituting grounds for divorce. Sections 452.320 and 452.305 require findings that the marriage is irretrievably broken and, where applicable, supporting facts, but provide no comparable joint waiver; Rule 73.01 addresses opinions and factual findings more generally.

norms.heading: Judgment

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon

norms.text:
(a) Included Matters. "Judgment" as used in these rules includes a decree and any order from which an appeal lies. A judgment is rendered when entered. A judgment is entered when a writing signed by the judge and denominated "judgment" or "decree" is filed. The judgment may be a separate document or entry on the docket sheet of the case. A docket sheet entry complying with these requirements is a judgment unless the docket sheet entry indicates that the court will enter the judgment in a separate document. The separate document shall be the judgment when entered.
(b) Judgment Upon Multiple Claims or Involving Multiple Parties. When more than one claim for relief is presented in an action, whether as a claim, counterclaim, cross-claim, or third-party claim, or when multiple parties are involved, the court may enter a judgment as to one or more but fewer than all of the claims or parties only upon an express determination that there is no just reason for delay.
In the absence of such determination, any order or other form of decision, however designated, that adjudicates fewer than all the claims or the rights and liabilities of fewer than all the parties shall not terminate the action as to any of the claims or parties, and the order or other form of decision is subject to revision at any time before the entry of judgment adjudicating all the claims and the rights and liabilities of all the parties.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsqu’une décision n’est pas immédiatement susceptible de recours, elle peut être consignée par une simple mention au dossier ou au registre d’audience. La Rule 74.01(a) admet une inscription au docket sheet, mais exige qu’elle satisfasse aux conditions formelles applicables au jugement.
correspondences.note_en: When a ruling cannot be appealed independently, it may be recorded by a simple notation in the case file or hearing register. Rule 74.01(a) permits a docket-sheet entry, but requires compliance with the formal requirements applicable to a judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut l’opposition et reporte en principe l’appel ou le pourvoi contre les décisions d’exécution d’une mesure d’instruction au recours contre le jugement au fond; il précise aussi leurs formes. RSMo 512.020 permet généralement le contrôle des décisions interlocutoires avec le jugement final, tandis que la règle 74.01 définit notamment le jugement et l’inscription au rôle.
correspondences.note_en: The article bars opposition and generally defers appeal or cassation of decisions concerning the execution of an evidentiary measure until review of the merits judgment, while specifying their forms. RSMo 512.020 generally permits review of interlocutory rulings with the final judgment, and Rule 74.01 addresses judgments and docket-sheet entry.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge règle les difficultés d'exécution de la vérification et formalise sa décision par une mention au dossier, une ordonnance ou un jugement. Rule 74.01 reconnaît le jugement ou décret et son inscription, tandis que RSMo 511.650 organise certaines mentions au docket, sans régler la vérification d'écriture.
correspondences.note_en: The judge resolves implementation difficulties and records the decision by docket notation, order, or judgment. Rule 74.01 addresses judgments or decrees and their entry, while RSMo 511.650 specifies docket entries; neither governs handwriting verification itself.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confie au juge la décision sur le faux, tout en permettant de statuer séparément sur les autres chefs de demande. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le jugement selon le droit et la preuve ainsi que les jugements portant sur certaines demandes seulement, sans règle spécifique sur le faux documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns the forgery issue to the judge while allowing the remaining claims to be decided separately. Missouri rules address judgment under the law and evidence and judgments on fewer than all claims, but contain no specific rule for documentary forgery.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 453 fixe la date du jugement au jour de son prononcé. La Rule 74.01 rattache plutôt le jugement à son entrée, lorsque l’écrit signé est déposé; elle concerne donc la même question mais selon une technique différente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 453 fixes the judgment date as the date it is pronounced. Rule 74.01 instead ties judgment to entry when the signed writing is filed, addressing the same issue through a materially different mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 454 énumère les mentions obligatoires du jugement, notamment la juridiction, les juges, la date, le greffier et les parties. RSMo 511.650 impose certaines mentions au docket, tandis que la Rule 74.01 définit les conditions formelles d’entrée du jugement, sans reprendre l’ensemble des mentions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 454 lists required judgment particulars, including the court, judges, date, clerk, and parties. RSMo 511.650 requires certain docket entries, while Rule 74.01 sets formal requirements for entry of judgment; neither reproduces the full French list.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la signature du président et du greffier, prévoit le remplacement du président empêché et encadre la signature électronique qualifiée du jugement, avec une sanction de vice de forme. Les règles du Missouri reconnaissent les signatures du juge et du greffier, ainsi que les signatures électroniques, mais sans reprendre ces conditions ni cette sanction.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires signatures by the presiding judge and clerk, addresses an unavailable presiding judge, and regulates qualified electronic signatures, with a formal defect sanction. Missouri recognizes judge and clerk signatures and electronic signatures, but does not reproduce these conditions or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article sanctionne par la nullité certaines irrégularités formelles du jugement et prévoit une limitation temporelle pour certaines objections. Les textes du Missouri traitent des imperfections du jugement, de leur correction et des conditions formelles d’entrée du jugement, mais leurs effets et mécanismes diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: The article makes specified formal defects in a judgment grounds for nullity and limits the timing of certain objections. Missouri provisions address judgment imperfections, their correction, and formal entry requirements, but use different mechanisms and effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 475 interdit de statuer avant l’expiration du plus long délai de comparution et prévoit en principe un jugement unique contre tous les défendeurs. Le Missouri prévoit un jugement final unique et encadre les décisions concernant seulement certains participants, mais ces textes ne fixent pas le plus long délai de comparution prévu par l’article 475.
correspondences.note_en: Article 475 bars the court from ruling before the longest appearance period expires and generally requires one judgment against all defendants. Missouri provides for one final judgment and regulates decisions involving fewer than all parties, but these provisions do not establish Article 475’s longest appearance period.

correspondences.note_fr: Le jugement avant dire droit ne dessaisit pas le juge. Rule 75.01 maintient le contrôle du tribunal pendant trente jours et Rule 74.01(b) permet la révision d’une décision avant le jugement final; RSMo 210.635 prévoit expressément la rétention de compétence dans une matière particulière.
correspondences.note_en: An interlocutory judgment does not divest the judge of the case. Rule 75.01 preserves trial-court control for 30 days and Rule 74.01(b) permits revision before final judgment; RSMo 210.635 expressly provides for retained jurisdiction in a specific proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 606 permet le pourvoi immédiat contre un jugement statuant définitivement sur une partie du principal tout en ordonnant une mesure d’instruction ou provisoire. La Rule 74.01 traite des jugements partiels, mais exige en principe une détermination expresse qu’il n’existe aucune raison justifiant un délai, et le Missouri ne reprend pas cette combinaison précise.
correspondences.note_en: Article 606 permits immediate cassation review of a judgment deciding part of the merits while ordering an evidentiary or provisional measure. Rule 74.01 addresses partial judgments, but generally requires an express determination that there is no just reason for delay, and Missouri does not reproduce the precise combination.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article organise un dossier individuel contenant les actes, documents, décisions, représentants et, en procédure orale, les prétentions des parties. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le dépôt des actes, l'apparition des avocats, le dossier d'appel et l'inscription des jugements, mais non un dossier de greffe identique ni la consignation générale des prétentions orales.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes an individual case file containing documents, decisions, representatives, and oral claims. Missouri rules address filing papers, counsel appearances, appellate records, and judgment entries, but do not provide an identical clerk-maintained file or a general record of oral claims.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article exige un registre d'audience détaillé, indiquant notamment la composition de la formation, les parties présentes, le caractère public de l'audience, les incidents et les décisions. Les textes du Missouri ne prévoient pas ce registre général, mais règlent séparément l'inscription des décisions, les audiences publiques et certaines audiences à huis clos.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a detailed hearing register recording the judges, clerk, parties, attendance, publicity, incidents, and decisions. Missouri has no comparable general hearing register, but separately addresses recording decisions, open trials, and closed hearings in specified proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 794 limite l’autorité de la chose jugée au principal des ordonnances du juge de la mise en état, tout en prévoyant des exceptions. La Rule 74.01 traite de la finalité et de la révision des décisions, tandis que la Rule 55.08 mentionne la res judicata comme moyen de défense, sans reproduire ce régime précis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 794 limits the res judicata effect of case-management judge orders, subject to specified exceptions. Rule 74.01 addresses finality and revision of orders, while Rule 55.08 recognizes res judicata as an affirmative defense, but neither establishes the same specific regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux parties de demander une clôture partielle de l’instruction afin qu’un jugement soit rendu sur certaines prétentions, tandis que l’instance se poursuit pour le surplus. La Rule 66.02 autorise un procès séparé et la Rule 74.01(b) un jugement portant sur moins que toutes les demandes, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce mécanisme de césure consensuelle.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows all parties to request partial closure so that specified claims may be adjudicated while the remainder continues. Rule 66.02 permits separate trials and Rule 74.01(b) permits judgment on fewer than all claims, but neither reproduces the consensual partial-closure mechanism exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: Le jugement partiel statue exclusivement sur les prétentions visées par la clôture partielle et peut être assorti de l’exécution provisoire. La Rule 74.01(b) permet un jugement sur une ou plusieurs demandes seulement, sous condition d’absence de raison justifiant le délai, et la Rule 74.04 permet un jugement sommaire sur tout ou partie des questions, dans le cadre particulier du summary judgment.
correspondences.note_en: The partial judgment decides only the claims covered by the partial closure and may be made provisionally enforceable. Rule 74.01(b) permits judgment on fewer than all claims subject to an express no-just-reason-for-delay finding, while Rule 74.04 permits summary judgment on all or part of the issues in its specific summary-judgment context.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confère à certaines ordonnances du conseiller de la mise en état l’autorité de la chose jugée au principal. La Rule 74.01 distingue les jugements et les ordonnances susceptibles d’appel et limite la révision des décisions partielles, sans prévoir cette liste ni cette institution française.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives specified case-management orders res judicata effect on the merits. Rule 74.01 distinguishes judgments from appealable orders and governs partial adjudications, but does not create this list or French case-management institution; Rule 74.02 merely defines an order.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut en principe le recours indépendant contre les ordonnances du conseiller, tout en permettant un déféré dans les quinze jours pour certaines catégories. La Rule 81.04 permet l’appel d’un jugement, décret ou ordonnance lorsqu’il est légalement ouvert, dans les dix jours de sa décision définitive; la Rule 74.01 traite de la finalité, et la Rule 84.035 prévoit un recours sur autorisation dans un domaine particulier.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally bars an independent appeal from case-management orders but permits referral within fifteen days for specified categories. Rule 81.04 permits an appeal from a judgment, decree, or legally appealable order within ten days after finality; Rule 74.01 addresses finality, while Rule 84.035 provides a specialized permission-to-appeal procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la signature de l’arrêt par le président, les rapporteurs et le greffier. La Rule 41.08 règle les modalités de signature des magistrats et du greffier, tandis que la Rule 74.01 exige la signature du juge pour un jugement, sans imposer cette combinaison de signatures.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the judgment to be signed by the president, reporting judge(s), and clerk. Rule 41.08 governs how judicial officers and clerks sign, and Rule 74.01 requires a judge’s signature for a judgment, but neither requires this specific combination of signatures.

norms.heading: Notice of Entry of Orders and Judgments

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon

norms.text: Immediately upon the entry of an order or judgment, the clerk shall serve a notice of the entry by mail in the manner provided for in Rule 43.01 upon each party who is not in default for failure to appear and who was not present in court in person or by attorney at the time of the entry of such order or judgment. If such notice is not given, the order or judgment shall be set aside for good cause shown upon written motion filed within six months from the entry of the order or judgment. This Rule 74.03 shall not preclude relief under Rule 74.06.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 478 rend certains jugements non avenus s’ils ne sont pas notifiés dans les six mois et permet de reprendre la procédure. La Rule 74.03 prévoit une notification immédiate et une possibilité d’annulation dans les six mois, mais seulement sur motion et pour bonne cause, sans reprise automatique de l’instance.
correspondences.note_en: Article 478 makes certain judgments ineffective if not notified within six months and permits recommencement of the proceedings. Rule 74.03 requires prompt notice and allows setting aside within six months for good cause, but only on motion and without the same automatic recommencement mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige la motivation, l’exécution au seul vu de la minute et la remise d’une copie de la requête et de l’ordonnance à la personne concernée. Le Missouri prévoit la motivation et l’entrée au dossier des mesures ex parte, ainsi que des règles de notification, sans reprendre exactement l’exécution sur minute.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires reasons, enforceability upon production of the original, and delivery of the application and order to the affected person. Missouri requires stated facts or reasons, filing and entry of ex parte orders, and notification mechanisms, but does not exactly replicate enforcement on the original.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la remise ou notification du certificat ou de la décision, certaines notifications spéciales et la conservation des pièces au greffe. Le Missouri prévoit la notification des décisions et jugements ainsi que la preuve de la signification, mais pas ce régime spécifique de certificats transfrontaliers.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs delivery or notification of the certificate or decision, special notices, and retention of documents by the clerk. Missouri provides notice of decisions and judgments and proof of service, but not this specific cross-border certificate regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 511 fixe le point de départ du délai de grâce selon le caractère contradictoire du jugement ou sa notification. La Rule 44.01 régit le calcul général des délais, tandis que la Rule 74.03 prévoit la notification de l’entrée du jugement, sans reprendre exactement cette distinction.
correspondences.note_en: Article 511 sets the starting point for the grace period depending on whether the judgment was adversarial or notified. Rule 44.01 provides general time-computation rules, while Rule 74.03 addresses notice of entry, without reproducing the same distinction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 586 fixe la durée et le point de départ de la tierce opposition, avec des délais particuliers après notification. Les RSMo 511.180 et 511.190 prévoient des délais de recours après notification ou après le jugement; les Rules 74.03 et 74.06 prévoient aussi des délais liés à la notification et à la remise en cause du jugement, mais pour d’autres recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 586 establishes limitation periods and triggering events for third-party opposition, including special periods after notice. RSMo 511.180 and 511.190 provide time limits for judgment review, while Rules 74.03 and 74.06 contain notice-related and judgment-relief deadlines for different remedies.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose en principe la notification des actes au représentant de la partie représentée, sous réserve des règles relatives aux jugements. La Rule 43.01(b) impose généralement le service à l’avocat, avec certaines exceptions; la Rule 74.03 règle spécialement la notification de l’entrée des jugements.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires documents for a represented party to be served on the representative, subject to special rules for judgments. Rule 43.01(b) generally requires service on the attorney, subject to exceptions, while Rule 74.03 specifically addresses notice of entry of judgments.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose en principe la signification des jugements et prévoit, en matière gracieuse, une notification par le greffier en lettre recommandée avec AR. La Rule 74.03 impose au greffier un avis d’entrée, mais seulement à certaines parties et selon les modalités de la Rule 43.01.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires formal service of judgments and provides for clerk notification by registered mail in non-contentious matters. Rule 74.03 requires the clerk to serve notice of entry, but only on specified parties and under the methods in Rule 43.01.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige que les jugements soient notifiés aux parties elles-mêmes. La Rule 43.01 prévoit en principe la notification à l’avocat de la partie représentée, tandis que la Rule 74.03 vise chaque partie non défaillante dans les conditions qu’elle énonce.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires judgments to be notified directly to the parties. Rule 43.01 generally serves the attorney of a represented party, while Rule 74.03 covers each non-defaulting party only under its stated conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 678 impose, en cas de représentation obligatoire, une information préalable du représentant avant la notification du jugement à la partie, avec une sanction de nullité et une règle spéciale en cas de décès ou cessation de fonctions. La Rule 74.03 prévoit la notification de l'entrée du jugement, et la Rule 43.01 organise le service à l'avocat, mais sans ces mêmes conditions ni effets.
correspondences.note_en: Article 678 requires, when representation is mandatory, prior notice to the representative before notice of the judgment to the party, with invalidity and special rules for death or cessation of functions. Rule 74.03 provides notice of entry of judgment, and Rule 43.01 governs service on counsel, but neither contains the same conditions or effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la forme des mesures du juge de la mise en état : simple mention au dossier avec avis aux avocats, ou ordonnance motivée dans certains cas. Les Rules 74.02 et 74.03 distinguent les ordres écrits et imposent la notification de leur entrée, sans reprendre le régime de la simple mention ni l’exigence générale de motivation.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs the form of case-management measures: a docket notation with notice to counsel, or a reasoned order in specified cases. Rules 74.02 and 74.03 address written orders and notice of their entry, but do not reproduce the French distinction between docket notation and reasoned orders.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 798 prévoit une ordonnance de clôture non motivée, insusceptible de recours, dont copie est délivrée aux avocats. Les règles 74.03 et 43.01 organisent la notification et le service des ordonnances, mais ne prévoient pas cette clôture ni son régime d’absence de recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 798 provides an unreasoned, non-appealable order closing the proceedings, with a copy delivered to counsel. Rules 74.03 and 43.01 govern notice and service of orders, but not this closure procedure or its non-appealability.

correspondences.note_fr: Les mesures sont en principe mentionnées au dossier et notifiées aux parties, tandis que certaines décisions prennent la forme d'une ordonnance motivée. La Rule 74.03 impose la notification de l'entrée des ordres et jugements, mais ne reprend pas le régime français de simple mention au dossier ni l'exigence générale de motivation.
correspondences.note_en: Measures are generally noted in the case file and communicated to the parties, while specified decisions take the form of reasoned orders. Rule 74.03 requires notice of entered orders and judgments, but does not reproduce the French system of docket notation or the general requirement of reasons.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 913-4 prévoit l’absence de recours contre les mesures du conseiller, avec des exceptions soumises à une ordonnance motivée et à des modalités particulières de recours, ainsi qu’une information des avocats. RSMo 512.020 énumère certaines décisions susceptibles d’appel et la Rule 74.03 organise la notification de l’entrée des ordonnances, mais sans reprendre ce régime spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 913-4 makes the case-management judge’s measures generally unreviewable, subject to specified exceptions, reasoned orders, and notice to counsel. RSMo 512.020 lists certain appealable orders, while Rule 74.03 governs notice of entry of orders, but neither establishes the same specific review regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la notification par le greffe des décisions de cassation, de rejet ou de cassation sans renvoi, selon la représentation des parties et le type de décision. Les Rules 84.16 et 84.026 prévoient la remise ou la signification de décisions et actes d’appel, tandis que la Rule 74.03 concerne les avis d’entrée des jugements, avec des conditions et modalités différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs clerk notification of cassation, dismissal, and cassation-without-remand decisions, depending on representation and disposition. Rules 84.16 and 84.026 address furnishing or serving appellate decisions and filings, while Rule 74.03 concerns notice of entry of judgments, with materially different conditions and methods.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffe la notification des décisions du juge à des destinataires déterminés, selon des modalités privilégiant la lettre recommandée, avec possibilité d’acte d’huissier ou de remise d’une copie certifiée contre récépissé. Les Rules 74.03 et 43.01 organisent la notification des ordonnances et jugements, mais selon des destinataires, formes et effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to notify specified recipients of the judge’s decision, generally by registered mail, while allowing service by bailiff or certified-copy delivery against receipt. Rules 74.03 and 43.01 govern notice and service of orders and judgments, but with different recipients, methods, and effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre la modification ou le renforcement d’une mesure après audition ou convocation de la personne protégée, prise en compte de l’avis du protecteur et notification de la décision. Le Missouri prévoit la modification ou le renouvellement après notification et audience, ainsi que la notification des ordres, mais dans des procédures différentes et selon d’autres conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs modification or strengthening of a protective measure after hearing or notice to the protected person, consideration of the protector’s view, and notification of the decision. Missouri provides modification or renewal after notice and hearing, and notice of orders, but in different protection proceedings and under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffe de notifier toute décision à un ensemble déterminé de personnes, notamment celles dont les droits sont modifiés et, sous conditions, au mineur. La Rule 74.03 prévoit la notification de l’entrée des jugements aux parties absentes, tandis que la Rule 43.01 fixe les destinataires du service des actes, sans reprendre les catégories particulières de protection.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to notify decisions to specified persons, including those whose rights are affected and, subject to conditions, a minor. Rule 74.03 requires notice of entry of judgments to absent nondefault parties, while Rule 43.01 governs recipients of service without reproducing the article’s protection-specific categories.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception, l’acte d’huissier sur décision du juge et la notification par remise certifiée avec information sur les recours. Les Rules 43.01 et 74.03 permettent principalement le service ou l’avis par courrier et d’autres moyens, tandis que la Rule 54.20 concerne la preuve du service.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for registered mail with acknowledgment, service by a bailiff at the judge’s direction, and certified delivery with information about remedies. Rules 43.01 and 74.03 principally allow service or notice by mail and other methods, while Rule 54.20 addresses proof of service.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la notification d’une décision de placement au requérant et au majeur protégé, sa transmission au procureur et l’absence de recours. La Rule 74.03 impose la notification de l’entrée d’une ordonnance ou d’un jugement aux parties, mais ne règle ni la transmission au procureur ni l’absence de recours.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires notice of the placement decision to the applicant and protected adult, transmission to the prosecutor, and no appeal. Rule 74.03 requires notice of entry of an order or judgment to parties, but does not address prosecutorial transmission or the bar on appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffe de notifier la décision par lettre recommandée avec demande d’avis de réception, en écartant une règle générale de notification. La Rule 74.03 impose au greffier l’envoi d’un avis d’entrée du jugement, mais sans reprendre exactement le même mode ni le même champ d’application.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to notify the decision by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt, displacing a general notification rule. Rule 74.03 requires the clerk to mail notice of entry of an order or judgment, but differs in method and scope.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe notifie l’ordonnance aux parties par lettre recommandée avec demande d’avis de réception et rappelle certains recours. La Rule 74.03 impose au greffier une notification de l’entrée de l’ordonnance ou du jugement par courrier, mais ne prévoit ni nécessairement le recommandé avec AR ni le contenu particulier de la notification.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk must notify the parties of the order by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt and mention specified remedies. Rule 74.03 requires the clerk to mail notice of entry of an order or judgment, but does not necessarily require registered mail with acknowledgment or the specified notice content.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confère à la sentence l’autorité de la chose jugée, permet l’exécution provisoire et prévoit sa notification. Le Missouri définit le jugement, prévoit l’exécution d’une sentence soumise à arbitrage et règle la notification et la signification des jugements et actes, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas l’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives the arbitral award res judicata effect, permits provisional enforcement, and requires notice. Missouri defines a judgment, addresses enforcement of an award submitted to arbitration, and governs notice and service of judgments and papers, but the supplied texts do not provide for provisional enforcement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe des délais précis pour demander la rectification ou le complément et impose la notification de la sentence rectificative selon les mêmes formes. Les règles 74.06 et 75.01 prévoient certains délais de correction des jugements, tandis que les règles 74.03 et 43.01 encadrent leur notification et leur signification, sans reprendre les délais ni le contexte arbitral.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets specific deadlines for correction or completion and requires the corrected award to be notified in the same manner as the original. Rules 74.06 and 75.01 provide some correction deadlines, while Rules 74.03 and 43.01 govern notice and service, but do not reproduce the arbitral context or exact time limits.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la cour d’appel compétente, permet le recours dès le prononcé et prévoit un délai d’un mois à compter de la notification. Les règles du Missouri organisent l’appel après la finalité du jugement, dans un délai de dix jours, avec notification de l’entrée du jugement et une procédure limitée d’appel tardif, sans règle équivalente sur la compétence territoriale liée au lieu du prononcé.
correspondences.note_en: The article identifies the competent court, allows review immediately upon issuance, and sets a one-month period from notification. Missouri rules provide for appeal after the judgment becomes final, generally within ten days, with notice of entry and a limited late-appeal procedure, but no equivalent venue rule tied to where the award was rendered.

correspondences.note_fr: La décision est notifiée par le greffe aux parties et à l’intervenant, avec possibilité d’une simple mention au dossier pour la conciliation. La Rule 74.03 impose au greffier de notifier l’entrée d’une ordonnance ou d’un jugement aux parties, mais ne vise pas spécifiquement le conciliateur ou le médiateur et ne prévoit pas cette forme simplifiée.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk must notify the parties and the neutral of the decision, while a conciliator appointment may appear as a simple docket entry. Rule 74.03 requires notice of entry of an order or judgment to the parties, but does not specifically address the neutral or provide the same simplified form.

norms.heading: Summary Judgment

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon

norms.text:
(a) For Claimant. At any time after the expiration of thirty days from the commencement of the action or after service of a motion for summary judgment by the adverse party, a party seeking to recover upon a claim, counterclaim, or cross-claim or to obtain a declaratory judgment may move with or without supporting affidavits for a summary judgment upon all or any part of the pending issues.
(b) For Defending Party. At any time, a party against whom a claim, counterclaim, or cross-claim is asserted or a declaratory judgment is sought may move with or without supporting affidavits for a summary judgment as to all or any part of the pending issues.

(c) Motions and Proceedings Thereon.
(1) Motions for Summary Judgment. A motion for summary judgment shall summarily state the legal basis for the motion.
A statement of uncontroverted material facts shall be attached to the motion. The statement shall state with particularity in separately numbered paragraphs each material fact as to which movant claims there is no genuine issue, with specific references to the pleadings, discovery, exhibits or affidavits that demonstrate the lack of a genuine issue as to such facts.
An electronic copy of the statement of uncontroverted material facts in a commonly used medium, such as a diskette, CD-ROM or e-mail attachment, in a format that can be read by most commonly used word processing programs, such as Word for Windows or WordPerfect 5.x or higher, shall be served on the party to whom the motion for summary judgment is directed. In addition to the information normally in a certificate of service, the certificate of service shall also state the format of the electronic copy and the medium used to transmit the electronic copy to the responding party.
Attached to the statement shall be a copy of all discovery, exhibits or affidavits on which the motion relies.

Movant shall file a separate legal memorandum explaining why summary judgment should be granted.

(2) Responses to Motions for Summary Judgment. Within 30 days after a motion for summary judgment is served, the adverse party shall serve a response on all parties. The response shall set forth each statement of fact in its original paragraph number and immediately thereunder admit or deny each of movant's factual statements.
A denial may not rest upon the mere allegations or denials of the party's pleading. Rather, the response shall support each denial with specific references to the discovery, exhibits or affidavits that demonstrate specific facts showing that there is a genuine issue for trial.

Attached to the response shall be a copy of all discovery, exhibits or affidavits on which the response relies.
A response that does not comply with this Rule 74.04(c)(2) with respect to any numbered paragraph in movant's statement is an admission of the truth of that numbered paragraph.

The response may also set forth additional material facts that remain in dispute, which shall be presented in consecutively numbered paragraphs and supported in the manner prescribed by Rule 74.04(c)(1).
An electronic copy of the response shall be served as provided in Rule 74.04(c)(1).

The response may include a legal memorandum explaining the legal or factual reasons why summary judgment should not be granted.

(3) Replies in Support of Motions for Summary Judgment. Within 15 days after service of the response, the movant may file a reply memorandum of law explaining why summary judgment should be granted.
Within the same time, if the adverse party's response sets forth additional material facts that remain in dispute, movant shall set forth each additional statement of fact in its original paragraph number and immediately thereunder admit or deny each such factual statement. Denials shall be supported in the manner prescribed by Rule 74.04(c)(2).
Within the same time, the movant may file a statement of additional material facts as to which movant claims there is no genuine issue. The statement shall be presented in consecutively numbered paragraphs and supported in the manner prescribed by Rule 74.04(c)(1).

An electronic copy of the reply shall be served as provided in Rule 74.04(c)(1).
Attached to the supplemental statement shall be a copy of any additional discovery, exhibits or affidavits on which the supplemental statement relies.
(4) Sur-replies in Opposition to Motions for Summary Judgment. Within 15 days of service, if movant files a statement of additional material facts pursuant to Rule 74.04(c)(3), the adverse party shall file a sur-reply. The sur-reply shall set forth each additional statement of fact in its original paragraph number and immediately thereunder admit or deny each such factual statement. The sur-reply shall be in the form and shall be supported in the manner prescribed by Rule 74.04(c)(2).
An electronic copy of the sur-reply shall be served as provided in Rule 74.04(c)(1).

Attached to the sur-reply shall be a copy of any additional discovery, exhibits or affidavits on which the sur-reply relies.

A sur-reply that does not comply with Rule 74.04(c)(2) with respect to any numbered paragraph in movant's statement of additional material facts is an admission of the truth of that numbered paragraph.
If the movant files a statement of additional material facts, the adverse party may file within the same time a sur-reply memorandum of law explaining the legal or factual reasons why summary judgment should not be granted.

(5) Additional papers. No other papers with respect to the motion for summary judgment shall be filed without leave of court.
(6) Rulings on Motions for Summary Judgment. After the response, reply and any sur-reply have been filed or the deadlines therefor have expired, the court shall decide the motion.

If the motion, the response, the reply and the sur-reply show that there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law, the court shall enter summary judgment forthwith.
A summary judgment, interlocutory in character, may be entered on any issue, including the issue of liability alone, although there is a genuine issue as to the amount of the damages.
(d) Case Not Fully Adjudicated on Motion. If on motion under this Rule 74.04 judgment is not entered upon the whole case or for all the relief asked and a trial is necessary, the court by examining the pleadings and the evidence before it, by interrogating counsel, and by conducting a hearing, if necessary, shall ascertain, if practicable, what material facts exist without substantial controversy and what material facts are actually and in good faith controverted.
The court shall thereupon make an order specifying the facts that appear without substantial controversy, including the extent to which the amount of damages or other relief is not in controversy, and directing such further proceedings in the action as are just. Upon the trial of the action the facts so specified shall be deemed established, and the trial shall be conducted accordingly.
(e) Form of Affidavit. Supporting and opposing affidavits shall be made on personal knowledge, shall set forth such facts as would be admissible in evidence, and shall show affirmatively that the affiant is competent to testify to the matters stated therein. Sworn or certified copies of all papers or parts thereof referred to in an affidavit shall be attached thereto or served therewith.
(f) When Affidavits Are Unavailable. Should it appear from the affidavits of a party opposing the motion that for reasons stated in the affidavits facts essential to justify opposition to the motion cannot be presented in the affidavits, the court may refuse the application for judgment or may order a continuance to permit affidavits to be obtained or depositions to be taken or discovery to be had or may make such other order as is just.
(g) Affidavit Made in Bad Faith. Should it appear to the satisfaction of the court at any time that any affidavit presented pursuant to this Rule 74.04 is presented in bad faith or solely for the purpose of delay, the court shall forthwith order the party presenting it to pay to the other party the amount of the reasonable expenses that the filing of the affidavit caused the other party to incur, including reasonable attorney's fees, and any offending party or attorney may be adjudged guilty of contempt.

committee_notes:
Committee Note – 1959

This rule is the same as Rule 56 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure with the amendments to paragraphs (c) and (e) recommended by the Federal Advisory Committee in 1955; and with the addition of paragraph (h) to make clear that the procedure is not applicable where there is a factual issue to be determined by the court or jury. The reasons for the amendments to paragraphs (c) and (e) are stated by the Federal Advisory Committee as follows:
"Subdivision (c). The specific provision, made by the amendment, allowing summary judgment to be granted against the party who has moved therefore, is in accord with N.Y.C.P. Rule 113 and Wis. Stat. Sec. 270.635(3) (1951), as well as the urging of commentators.
McDonald, Summary Judgments, 30 Tex. L. Rev. 285, 303 (1952); Clark, The Summary Judgment, 36 Minn. L. Rev. 567, 570-571 (1952); Comment, Summary Judgment, 25 Wash. L. Rev. 71, 76-77 (1950).
It codifies a result already achieved by most federal courts. See 6 Moore's Federal Practice Par. 56.12 (2d ed. 1953); 3 Barron & Holtzoff, Fed. Prac. & Proc. § 1235 (1950) [

See now, Wright, Federal Practice and Procedure: Civil].
"Subdivision (e). Some recent cases, particularly in the Third Circuit, have held that a mere allegation in the pleading is sufficient to create a genuine issue as to a material fact, and thus prevent summary judgment, even though the pleader has made no attempt to controvert affidavits and other evidentiary matter presented by his opponent; e. g.,
Frederick Hart & Co. v. Recordgraph Corp., 169 F.2d 580, 581 (3d Cir. 1948); Reynolds Metals Co. v. Metals Disintegrating Co., 8 F.R.D. 349 (D.N.J.1948), *aff'd*176 F.2d 90 (3d Cir.
1949); Chappell v. Goltsman, 186 F.2d 215, 218 (5th Cir. 1950); and cases cited in 6 Moore's Federal Practice Par. 56.11[3], n. 16 (2d ed. 1953).
This line of cases is termed "patently erroneous" in Note, 99 U. of Pa. L. Rev. 212, 214-215 (1950), citing many contrary authorities. The purpose of Rule 56 is to pierce the formal allegations of the pleadings and reach immediately the merits of the controversy.
If pleading allegations are sufficient to raise a genuine issue as against uncontradicted evidentiary matter, this remedy then becomes substantially without utility. Engl v. Aetna Life Ins. Co., 139 F.2d 469, 473 (2d Cir. 1943). The view of most cases and commentators is that, where the motion for summary judgment is supported by depositions or affidavits, the opposing party must make a similar presentation to show the existence of a genuine issue of fact, or suffer judgment to be entered.
3 Barron & Holtzoff, Fed. Prac. & Proc. § 1235 (1950) [ See, now, Wright Federal Practice and Procedure: Civil]. 6 Moore's Federal Practice 56.11[??], n. 21 (2d ed. 1953), and cases there cited; id. at 56.15[??]; Asbill & Snell, Summary Judgment Under the Federal Rules--When An Issue of Fact Is Presented, 51 Mich.
L. Rev. 1143, 1159-1165 (1953); Shientag, The Summary Judgment 24 (1941); Kennedy, The Federal Summary Judgment Rule, 13 Brooklyn L. Rev. 5 (1947); Comm., "Genuineness" of Issues on Summary Judgment, 4 Fed. Rules Serv. 940.
"The amendment to subdivision (e) states this last principle and thus makes it clear that pleading allegations cannot, in themselves, create a genuine issue of material fact when summary judgment is sought. By emphasizing the function of the motion for summary judgment, the amendment may stimulate more frequent and effective use of this device, as urged by the Judicial Conference of the United States, in its Report of Sept.1948, pp. 36-37, and by commentators.
Yankwich, Summary Judgment under Federal Practice, 40 Calif. L. Rev. 204 (1952); Clark, Special Problems in Drafting and Interpreting Procedural Codes and Rules, 3 Vand. L. Rev. 493, 502-505 (1950); Clark, The Summary Judgment, 36 Minn.
L. Rev. 567 (1952); Wright, Modern Pleading and the Pennsylvania Rules, 101 U. of Pa. L. Rev. 909, 936-937 (1953); Comment, Summary Judgment, 25 Wash. L. Rev. 71 (1950); Note, The Scope of Summary Judgment Under the Federal Rules, 5 Vand.
L. Rev. 607 (1952); Note, Summary Judgments in the Federal Courts, 99 U. of Pa. L. Rev. 212 (1950); see McAllister, Pre-Trial Practice in the Southern District of New York, 12 F.R.D. 373, 378.
Compare the holding that summary judgment granting specific performance can never be proper, for a party cannot be entitled to equitable relief as a matter of law, Seaboard Surety Co. v. Racine Screw Co., 203 F.2d 532 (7th Cir. 1953), with the grant of summary judgment of specific performance in
Dale v. Preg, 204 F.2d 434 (9th Cir. 1953), and Palmer v. Chamberlin, 191 F.2d 532, 27 A.L.R.2d 416 (5th Cir. 1951), and as expressly authorized in N.Y.C.P.
Rule 113. See also the grant of summary judgment of injunction in United States v. W. T. Grant Co., 345 U.S. 629, 73 S.Ct. 894, 97 L.Ed. 1303 (1953), and Houghton, Mifflin Co. v. Stackpole Sons, 113 F.2d 627 (2d Cir. 1940).
"The amended rule does not, of course, require the grant of summary judgment in a case where such judgment is not proper even though the facts be taken as in the moving party's affidavit.

"The court may deny the motion if for any reason summary judgment would be inappropriate, even though the opposite party has not submitted an affidavit. The court may order a continuance in accordance with the provisions of Rule 56(f) where a party makes a substantial showing by affidavit that he cannot then present the facts essential to justify his opposition to judgment."

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 15 impose une communication réciproque et en temps utile des moyens de fait, preuves et moyens de droit. Rule 56.01 organise la discovery, Rule 43.01 la notification des actes, et Rule 74.04 l’échange structuré des faits et pièces dans les requêtes en jugement sommaire, sans règle générale entièrement équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 15 requires timely mutual disclosure of factual grounds, evidence, and legal arguments. Rule 56.01 governs discovery, Rule 43.01 service of papers, and Rule 74.04 structured exchanges in summary-judgment proceedings, but no provision creates the same comprehensive general duty.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 16 impose au juge de faire respecter la contradiction et interdit de fonder sa décision sur des éléments non discutés, notamment les moyens relevés d’office. Les règles du Missouri prévoient des échanges, audiences et possibilités de réponse dans certaines procédures, sans énoncer une obligation générale aussi large.
correspondences.note_en: Article 16 requires the court to preserve adversarial debate and bars reliance on undisputed submissions, including unraised legal grounds without an opportunity to comment. Missouri rules provide responses, hearings, and opportunities to address materials in specified proceedings, but not the same broad general duty.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 499-1 permet d’accorder une provision pour le procès et de rejeter rapidement une demande manifestement infondée. La Rule 74.04 organise le summary judgment et les textes relatifs au rejet permettent certaines sorties anticipées, mais aucun ne prévoit ces pouvoirs spécifiques pour la participation au débat public.
correspondences.note_en: Article 499-1 permits a litigation advance and rapid dismissal of a manifestly unfounded claim. Rule 74.04 provides summary judgment, while the dismissal provisions allow some early dispositions, but none establishes these specific powers for public-debate participation.

norms.heading: Entry of Default Judgment

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon

norms.text:
(a) Entry of Default Judgment. When a party against whom a judgment for affirmative relief is sought has failed to plead or otherwise defend as provided by these rules, upon proof of damages or entitlement to other relief, a judgment may be entered against the defaulting party. The entry of an interlocutory order of default is not a condition precedent to the entry of a default judgment.
(b) Entry of Interlocutory Order of Default. When a party against whom a judgment for affirmative relief is sought has failed to plead or otherwise defend as provided by these rules, an interlocutory order of default may be entered against that party. After entry of an interlocutory order of default, a default judgment may be entered. Any party may demand a jury to assess damages. If a jury is not demanded, the court shall assess any damages.
(c) Default Judgment May Include. A default judgment may include an award of damages, other relief, or both.

(d) When Set Aside. Upon motion stating facts constituting a meritorious defense and for good cause shown, an interlocutory order of default or a default judgment may be set aside.

The motion shall be made within a reasonable time not to exceed one year after the entry of the default judgment.
"Good cause" includes a mistake or conduct that is not intentionally or recklessly designed to impede the judicial process.

An order setting aside an interlocutory order of default or a default judgment may be conditioned on such terms as are just, including a requirement that the party in default pay reasonable attorney fees and expenses incurred as a result of the default by the party who requested the default.
A motion filed under this Rule 74.05(d), even if filed within 30 days after judgment, is an independent action and not an authorized after-trial motion subject to Rule 78.04, 78.06, or 81.05.

correspondences.note_fr: En cas de non-comparution du défendeur cité à personne, le juge tient l'écrit pour reconnu. La Rule 74.05 prévoit plus généralement le jugement par défaut en cas de défaut de défense, tandis que la Rule 54.13 encadre la signification personnelle, sans prévoir la reconnaissance de l'écriture.
correspondences.note_en: If a personally served defendant fails to appear, the court treats the writing as acknowledged. Rule 74.05 more generally governs default for failure to defend, while Rule 54.13 governs personal service; neither specifically provides for deeming handwriting genuine.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 468 prévoit les effets de la non-comparution injustifiée du demandeur : jugement au fond, renvoi, caducité de la citation et relevé de caducité sous quinze jours. La Rule 67.03 permet le rejet pour défaut de poursuite ou de respect des règles, la Rule 74.05 le jugement par défaut, et la Rule 65.01 le renvoi, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble de ce régime.
correspondences.note_en: Article 468 addresses the plaintiff’s unjustified failure to appear, allowing a merits judgment, continuance, dismissal for lapse of the summons, and reinstatement within fifteen days. Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply, Rule 74.05 permits default judgment, and Rule 65.01 permits continuances, but none reproduces the full regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose que le juge statue au fond malgré la défaillance, en n’accordant la demande que si elle est régulière, recevable et bien fondée. La Rule 74.05 permet le jugement par défaut après preuve des dommages ou du droit à une autre réparation, mais le texte fourni ne reprend pas expressément les trois critères français.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a decision on the merits despite default, granting relief only when the claim is procedurally proper, admissible, and well-founded. Rule 74.05 permits default judgment upon proof of damages or entitlement to other relief, but the supplied text does not expressly state the French three-part test.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 474 détermine si, en présence de plusieurs défendeurs dont certains ne comparaissent pas, le jugement est réputé contradictoire ou rendu par défaut, selon l’appel possible et la citation à personne. Le Missouri permet un jugement par défaut contre certains défendeurs et la poursuite de l’instance contre les autres, mais ne reprend pas ces critères.
correspondences.note_en: Article 474 determines whether, when several defendants fail to appear, the judgment is treated as adversarial or rendered by default, depending on appealability and personal service. Missouri permits default judgment against some defendants while the action proceeds against the others, but does not reproduce those criteria.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 476 ouvre en principe l’opposition contre le jugement rendu par défaut, sauf exclusion expresse. La Rule 74.05 permet de faire annuler un jugement par défaut sur motion, sous conditions et dans un délai maximal d’un an; les autres textes offrent des mécanismes plus limités de remise en cause du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 476 generally allows opposition to a default judgment unless expressly excluded. Rule 74.05 permits a default judgment to be set aside by motion, subject to specified grounds and a one-year maximum, while the other provisions provide narrower forms of relief from judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition permet au défaillant de faire rétracter un jugement rendu par défaut. La Rule 74.05 et les §§ 511.170, 511.200 et 511.220 prévoient des mécanismes de remise en cause d'un jugement par défaut, mais avec des conditions, délais et fondements différents.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition allows the defaulting party to obtain retraction of a default judgment. Rule 74.05 and §§ 511.170, 511.200, and 511.220 provide mechanisms to challenge default judgments, but impose different conditions, time limits, and grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition saisit le même juge afin qu'il statue à nouveau en fait et en droit, le jugement initial ne disparaissant qu'en cas de rétractation. Les textes du Missouri permettent de faire annuler ou réexaminer le jugement par défaut et, selon le § 511.220, de reprendre l'instance comme si le défendeur avait comparu, sans reprendre exactement cette règle.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition returns the matter to the same judge for a new decision on fact and law, with the original judgment surviving unless retracted. Missouri provisions permit default-judgment relief and, under § 511.220, continuation as if the defendant had appeared, but do not reproduce the rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition est formée selon les formes de la demande, éventuellement par notification entre avocats ou déclaration au greffe, puis instruite selon la procédure applicable. La Rule 74.05 encadre la demande de remise en cause d'un jugement par défaut, tandis que les Rules 55.26, 55.02 et 55.03 fixent des exigences générales de forme, de présentation et de signature, sans prévoir la procédure française particulière.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition is brought in the form of an initiating claim, sometimes by attorney-to-attorney service or a declaration with the clerk, and proceeds under the applicable procedure. Rule 74.05 governs relief from default judgment, while Rules 55.26, 55.02, and 55.03 impose general motion, formatting, and signature requirements without reproducing the French procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une déclaration au greffe par l’avocat constitué et un délai d’un mois, à peine d’irrecevabilité. La Rule 74.05(d) prévoit une motion pour faire annuler un jugement par défaut dans un délai raisonnable, limité à un an, mais sans ces formalités ni ce délai précis.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires filing with the issuing court’s clerk through counsel within one month, on pain of inadmissibility. Rule 74.05(d) provides a motion to set aside default judgment within a reasonable time, capped at one year, but lacks the same filing formalities and deadline.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 613 diffère le pourvoi contre une décision par défaut jusqu’à l’expiration du délai d’opposition. La Rule 74.05 prévoit plutôt la mise à néant du jugement par défaut, tandis que les Rules 81.05 et 81.04 organisent la finalité et le délai de l’appel, sans règle identique sur l’opposition.
correspondences.note_en: Article 613 postpones review of a default decision until the period for opposition has expired. Rule 74.05 instead governs setting aside default, while Rules 81.05 and 81.04 govern finality and appeal timing without an identical opposition-before-review rule.

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon
